Fix: Apply an advanced audit policy on DCs (Microsoft or ANSSI baseline).
GPO: enable PowerShell Module Logging and Script Block Logging.
Back up AD (system state of a DC) on a regular basis and test the restore.
Disable SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 on DCs (SCHANNEL registry keys or GPO), keep TLS 1.2+.
Reset the krbtgt password twice, waiting for full replication between the two resets (Microsoft New-KrbtgtKeys.ps1 helps).
Deploy Windows LAPS so every local admin password is unique and rotated.
GPO on DCs: 'Domain controller: LDAP server signing requirements' = Require signing.
GPO: LAN Manager auth level = 'Send NTLMv2 only, refuse LM & NTLM' and 'Do not store LM hash' = Enabled.
Raise the minimum password length to 12+ chars in the domain policy and in every fine grained policy.
Deploy NetCease by GPO to stop session enumeration (BloodHound style recon).
Create a fine grained policy (20+ chars) for service accounts, or move them to gMSA.
Block anonymous access: set RestrictAnonymous = 1 and restrict anonymous access to named pipes and shares by GPO.
Remove 'Anonymous Logon' from 'Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access'.
Empty 'Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access'. It gives wide read access to AD.
Make sure the PDC runs 2012 R2+ so 'Protected Users' exists, then add Tier 0 admins to it.
Delete passwords stored in GPP files (cpassword) in SYSVOL, then change those passwords. The key is public.
Replace SHA1 intermediate certificates with SHA256 ones.
Replace SHA1 root certificates with SHA256 ones.
Rotate the hidden password of smart card accounts (toggle 'Smart card required' off then on), or enable automatic NTLM secret rolling (DFL 2016).
Clear userPassword / unixUserPassword attributes. Any user can often read them.
Remove or replace trusted certificates with RSA keys under 2048 bits.
Reset admin passwords and set a rotation rule. Old admin passwords are often already leaked or cracked.
Review ACLs on Tier 0 objects (domain root, AdminSDHolder, DCs OU). Remove rights given to Everyone / Authenticated Users.
Empty DnsAdmins. Members can load a DLL on DCs and become domain admin.
Remove write rights for Everyone / Authenticated Users on GPO files in SYSVOL. Only GPO admins should edit them.
Remove SPNs from admin accounts, or use gMSA. Admins with an SPN can be cracked offline.
Empty Account, Server, Print and Backup Operators. Use delegation instead.
Empty 'Allowed RODC Password Replication Group' unless you really cache secrets on RODCs.
Restore default members of 'Denied RODC Password Replication Group' (Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins...).
Keep Schema Admins empty. Add an account only during a schema change, then remove it.
Replace unconstrained delegation with constrained or resource based delegation. Mark admins 'sensitive and cannot be delegated'.
Set ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to 0 so normal users cannot join computers to the domain.
Set the primary group of computers back to 'Domain Computers' (515).
Migrate the Windows 2008 DC to a supported version, then demote it.
Clean the metadata of the dead DC (ntdsutil or ADUC) so replication and DNS stay clean.
Delete the DOMAIN$$$ audit group once SID History migration is over.
Enable Kerberos pre-authentication on admin accounts (blocks AS-REP roasting).
Upgrade or remove Windows 2008 servers. They get no security fixes.
Upgrade or isolate the Windows 7 machine. It gets no security fixes.
Remove 'Password never expires' from user accounts. Move service accounts to gMSA.
Clear SID History on accounts once migration is over.
Disable SMBv1 on all servers and clients. It is old and was used by WannaCry.
Delete trusts that are no longer used. An old trust is an open door to an unmanaged domain.
Enable SID filtering (quarantine) on external and forest trusts.
